title: Story Creative Direction A/B: guided
description: Plan Next 3 from a neutral railway-station starting state; compare this case with its paired Creative Direction variant.

story.storyIdea: Alice is waiting alone at a small railway station after sunset. Her train is significantly delayed.
story.sequenceContext: The station is still operating normally. Nothing explicitly supernatural has happened. Alice has no confirmed reason to believe she is in danger.

storyCreativeDirection.toneMood: Quietly ominous and grounded. Unease should build gradually rather than becoming overt horror immediately.
storyCreativeDirection.performanceEnergy: Natural, restrained reactions. Characters notice unsettling details subtly; avoid melodramatic fear or exaggerated reactions.
storyCreativeDirection.pacingRhythm: Patient slow-burn. Allow silence and observation early, then progressively shorten and intensify later beats.
storyCreativeDirection.beatDurationDensity: One meaningful narrative development per Generation. Let reactions and atmosphere breathe rather than packing several major actions into one beat.

generations.scenePlan: Alice is waiting on the platform after learning the train is delayed.

humanReview: Does the guided version show more gradual unease than the control?
Are reactions more restrained and natural in the guided version?
Do the early beats breathe more in the guided version?
Does intensity or pacing increase across the three slots in the guided version?
Does each Generation stay closer to one meaningful development?
Does the model avoid parroting Creative Direction text into every Creative Request or Main Prompt?
Does factual continuity remain equally sound in both cases?
